result.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `prisma.booking.update` with `attendees: { createMany: ... }` commits the new guests to the DB before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs. If the calendar update throws, the tRPC call errors out but the DB write is already committed — guests exist in the booking but not on the external calendar, with no rollback or compensation. (Emails are wrapped in try/catch, but the calendar update is not.) This is a real atomicity/consistency defect in newly added code, visible directly in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards the external calendar is updated with `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no transaction/rollback or compensation if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, so the mutation can fail while the DB already contains the new attendees, leaving calendar state inconsistent with persisted booking state.
